sub: Virtual servers in the cloud: lifecycle, Stop vs Terminate.

Overview.p: Amazon EC2 gives resizable virtual servers called instances. You pick the OS, CPU, memory, storage and network, and pay per second or hour.
A computer you rent by the hour. Stop it and compute billing stops; terminate it and it is gone.
A web shop runs its site on EC2, adds instances before a sale and stops them after to save money.
Stop = Pause • Terminate = Delete forever • Check the bill

items: Choose an instance type (CPU and RAM)
Set network, storage and security group
Connect with SSH or Session Manager

Practical.p: Terminate or delete everything you created after practice to avoid charges.

items: Allow SSH only from your IP, never 0.0.0.0/0
Use IAM roles instead of access keys on the server
Prefer SSM Session Manager over open SSH

Examples.p: run Apache or Nginx on EC2 behind a load balancer.
launch a server for a day and terminate it.
start many instances for a job and stop them after.

code: aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-0abcdef1234567890 --instance-type t3.micro --key-name my-key --security-group-ids sg-0abc123

CLI Commands.p: IDs like i-0abc123 and sg-0abc123 are examples. Replace them with your real IDs.

items: A service that gives resizable virtual servers in the cloud.
Stop pauses the instance (EBS kept, no compute charge). Terminate deletes it and, by default, its root volume.
Does the public IP stay after stop and start?
No. It changes unless you use an Elastic IP.
pending, running, stopping, stopped, shutting-down, terminated.
How do you connect to a Linux instance?
SSH with the key pair, EC2 Instance Connect, or SSM Session Manager.
EBS storage and Elastic IPs, not compute.
Instance states: pending, running, stopped, terminated
